final_answer: Hypothesis: There is a statistically significant difference in educational attainment between males and females in the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth (NLSY79) dataset. The context of the hypothesis is the relationship between gender and the highest grade completed by respondents in 1979. The variables chosen are "Sex of respondent, 1979" (gender) and "Highest grade completed, 1979" (educational attainment). The analysis revealed that females had a slightly higher mean highest grade completed (mean = 10.61) compared to males (mean = 10.38), and this difference was statistically significant (t = -5.69, p ≈ 1.29 × 10⁻⁸).
